methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DroneForge, a pre-seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Chester Zelaya, has raised $2.5M to date. The sector comprises eight known private companies—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables available for direct market-based valuation.

The valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression method, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($2.5M) as a proxy base value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Pre-Seed to the subsequent stage yields an implied valuation of $6M. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while seven same-sector companies exist, none met minimum thresholds for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient data density, making sector-wide medians unreliable for a pre-seed position.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, centered at $6M. This range reflects the mechanics of stage-progression modeling but carries material uncertainty given the single-method foundation. Key risks to valuation include the early-stage nature of the company, limited comparable transaction data at pre-seed in this sector, and the absence of disclosed financial metrics or product-market traction indicators. Investors should treat this range as directional rather than precise and update estimates as the company advances toward seed-stage financing with clearer operational milestones.
